name: Dhaval Packaging Limited
sector: IML plastic packaging and industrial end caps; proposed tin packaging
summary: Mixed-quality manufacturing watchlist, not a proven compounder or a confirmed bargain. FY 2026 operations 65.03 crore, PAT 8.04 and CFO 6.74 improved with utilization and in-house end-cap production. Yet cash after capex is negative, a 50.21 crore project enters unproven tin packaging, and repeated disclosure defects limit stewardship confidence. BQS/GQS are supportable medium-confidence assessments; IAS remains NS despite linked scenarios. [S1][S2]
identity_note: Issuer annual confirmsAugust 6 listing; prospectus/master shares 13,736,800 and lot 1200.
score_note: BQS/GQS medium-confidence; IAS NS despite explicit scenario model.

GOV.reason: Detailed related transactions and restatement bridges are available and remuneration modest relative to PAT. Repeated historical filing defects, unfinished procedural status, omitted annual annexure and supplier-interest disclosure weaknesses indicate limited controls. No diversion or critical integrity failure established; small TDS amount not decisive.

MOAT.reason: High utilization, IML tooling and retained manufacturing relationships provide operational competence. Customer/supplier concentration, related label supply and plastics competition limit evidence of durable pricing power; new tin capability unproven.

REV.reason: Three-year FY 2023–26 operations CAGR 14.85% falls 10–15% band; five-year primary anchor not available after issuer-directory/history search. Secondary FY 2021 sales 22.60 suggests 24% five-year but is not substituted for verified primary anchor. In-house end-cap shift improves retained economics; no adjustment for a single stronger annual period.

DUR.reason: High existing utilization and IPO-funded expansion support accessible runway, including customer-format demand. January 2027 commissioning, new tin products, machinery ordering and internal funding requirements prevent higher confidence in durable funded growth.

CAP.reason: Average returns are above 12–15% cost-of-capital sensitivity but incremental 13.64% is only around it after full capital/debt inclusion. Expansion capital and new tin line have no realized cohort return; high accounting ROE is not automatic reinvestment excellence.

CASH.reason: Three-year CFO/PAT 75.1% and improving FY 2026 cash generation support moderate conversion. Rising aged receivables, stocks, overdue charges and persistent negative post-capex cash constrain credit; cash not financed inside CFO as in some other issuers.

BAL.reason: IPO provides meaningful equity and debt-repayment funds; March leverage belowone times equity and interest coverage adequate. Most proceeds earmarked for larger project, cash deposits partly restricted and cash-credit/current maturities remain; no claim of unrestricted net cash.

EXEC.reason: Capacity use and in-house end-cap manufacture grew alongside core operating profit and CFO. New tin project not commissioned, procedural controls weak and latest milestone proof incomplete; no track record credit for proposed capacity.

EARN.reason: Profit growth 33.05% supported by volume/utilization, manufacturing mix and small other income. Stock credit increased 0.8675 crore and trade-to-manufacturing cost changes complicate margin persistence; prior-year accounting adjustments are disclosed, not ignored.

L.reason: Observed secondary liquidity supports about 3.3 active-session exit at 5% using lower-bound median, but one lot 28.08% of position and short trading history limit implementation. No live BSE depth or named restrictions clearance; conditional score not unrestricted exit assurance.

R.reason: Linked sensitivities are supplied but new tin economics, current project deployment and live execution evidence remain low-confidence. Do not convert assumed terminal multiples into supported attractiveness scores. Reassessed against the corrected opening-claim cash/debt cases dated 20 October 2026; the identified material evidence gaps remain, so this factor is still NS.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Mixed-quality manufacturing watchlist, not a proven compounder or a confirmed bargain. FY 2026 operations 65.03 crore, PAT 8.04 and CFO 6.74 improved with utilization and in-house end-cap production. Yet cash after capex is negative, a 50.21 crore project enters unproven tin packaging, and repeated disclosure defects limit stewardship confidence. BQS/GQS are supportable medium-confidence assessments; IAS remains NS despite linked scenarios. [S1][S2]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Dhaval Packaging Limited, BSE SME code 544854/DHAVAL, ISIN INE1HX301016, listed 6 August 2026. Not Dhaval Exports. Incorporated 2015 following legacy Dhaval Corporation activity; standalone only, no subsidiary/associate.13.7368 million postIPO face 10 shares and 1200-share market lot, not 2400-share minimum IPO application. Five-year 15% nominal pre-tax hurdle, illustrative Rs 5 lakh position. Financial cutoffMarch 2026 plus dated IPO/Septemberannual; observed secondary quote 19 October 117. [S1][S2][S6][S7] Secondary 19 October close 117; official lot 1200 costs 140400 or 28.08% of a Rs 5 lakh position.50 observed dated rowsAugust 7–October 19; listingAugust 6 missing in source and never filled as a zero.20-observation low×volume median 30.264 lakh implies 3.30 observed-active sessions at 5% participation; at 2% about 8.26 and 10% about 1.65. These conservative price×volume proxies are not exchange turnover or live executable depth. BSE restrictions and spreads unverified, so L5 is conditional and no universal clearance is claimed. [S1][S6][S7]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS 5.18; GQS 5.75; IAS NS. Canonical factor evidence, weights, unrounded arithmetic and bounds are recorded in factor_audit and score_audit. R/D/P are not scoreable because tin-line economics and funded execution are unproven; L 5 is conditional on secondary observed activity. No missing weight is redistributed. [S1][S2][S7]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Plastic IML packaging serves food/FMCG customers; pipe-end caps serve industrial customers. Tooling, label/process quality and customer formats support operating relationships, but do not prove permanent pricing power. Top 10 customers 51.27%, largest 10.07%; top 10 suppliers 88.31%. Octa Labels is a material related supplier. End caps moved from trading toward own manufacture, so gross-margin comparisons reflect integration as well as procurement. New tin containers are prospective, not historical competence. [S1][S2]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Existing IML tooling, 90% capacity utilization and established customer relationships provide operating evidence, but do not establish pricing power or a durable franchise. Largest customer is 10.07% and top ten 51.27%, reducing single-buyer risk versus concentrated project SMEs. Top ten suppliers are 88.31%, related label procurement is substantial, and the new tin line has no proven competitive economics. MOAT 5 reflects these offsets, not a moat claim from utilization alone. [S1][S2]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: FY 2022/23 operations 33.2373/42.9365 crore, original PAT 0.1656/0.2446. FY 2023 restated PAT 0.5089 is reconciled through depreciation, gratuity and taxes in the draft prospectus. FY 2024/25/26 operations 47.9932/52.2628/65.0318 and restated PAT 1.5511/6.0422/8.0389. FY 2024 original PAT 1.6910 becomes 1.5511; FY 2025/26 PAT unchanged. Restated equity rises 0.1083 crore for deferred-tax balance, not hidden operating profit. Do not mix current-share EPS 5.85 with weighted historical 8.08 or assume bonus shares create economic growth. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5] Verified three-year revenue CAGR 14.85% is used because a primary FY 2021 anchor was not found in issuer directory/search; secondary 22.60 crore FY 2021 is disclosed as an unverified alternative, not selectively adopted. FY 2026 growth 24.43% includes 17.93% IML and 46.22% end caps. Total current capacity 8400 kg/day, actual 7560 or 90%, versus 84.73% prior. Proposed facility adds IML/end-cap capacity and tin packaging; weights of polymer versus metal capacity are not directly equivalent revenues. Customer conversion, ramp rates and new-product economics must be demonstrated. [S1][S2][S3][S8]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Full restated equity+debt-cash IC is 51.8701 crore versus 34.7843. Core NOPAT at 25% tax over average IC yields 21.45%, but incremental NOPAT/IC only 13.64%, near the analyst 12–15% cost-of-capital sensitivity. Including restricted deposits instead of subtracting all cash further reduces returns. FY 2026 cash capex 14.1595 includes 6.2263 building CWIP addition, not just operating-machine replacement. New project capital 50.2123 crore needs cohort returns, not an extrapolation of accounting ROE. [S1][S2] Fresh IPO gross 36.3034/net 32.4501 crore funds 27.1902 project,3.75 debt and 1.5099 GCP. Project 50.2123 had 15.7564 spentJuly 1, with 7.2657 more internal funding alongside IPO. March debt 24.1316 includes 3.7543 current maturities; gross cash 3.0092 is not all usable due LC/DSRA and other bank FDs. Model uses only cash/current bank 1.0993, excluding all deposits. January 2027 commercial production remains a target; prospectus machinery quotations were not yet definitive orders even though schedule assumed July ordering. Verify actual installation and postIPO use, rather than declaring current net cash. [S1][S2]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Repeated statutory filing defects, missing/unsigned historical documents and a voluntary NCLT revision petition show control weaknesses; the prospectus says the procedural petition does not change figures. August 20 hearing was prospective at filing; subsequent disposition not verified. Separate accounting restatements have explicit bridges. September 11 corrected omission of employee annexure, not financial economics. Related label purchases 6.6099 crore, prior connected asset purchases 2.76 crore and director loans merit scrutiny; five director salaries 0.485775 crore are modest relative to PAT. Unmodified audit is not blanket reassurance. No verified integrity fail or diversion established, and 0.025 crore TDS contingency alone is economically immaterial. [S1][S2][S4]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY 2024–26 CFO 0.6571,4.3471,6.7392 and capex 4.1070,10.7566,14.1595 crore produce three-year CFO/PAT 75.1% but persistent negative cash after investment. FY 2026 net cash movement reconciles. Stocks 14.2057 and receivables 8.3073 including noncurrent balances have grown;6–12 month ageing 1.2997 versus 0.3436 and older 0.2737 require collections testing. Reclassification to noncurrent is not a loss allowance. Finished-stock credit rose 0.8675 crore, a meaningful but partial driver of profit growth. Overdue-payment charges 0.8173 already depress earnings; do not deduct twice. [S1][S2]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At 117,13.7368 million shares imply 160.7206 crore market cap, trailing current-share P/E19.99. March restated book multiple 5.23 falls to about 2.54 after simply adding netIPO proceeds, before subsequent profits/expenses, illustrating why a dated bridge matters. Linked five-year models retain actual opening debt/cash/WC, charge remaining project spend and maintenance, model 11% interest on gross debt and additional funding, then EV/EBITDA-to-equity. Bear/base/bull EBIT margins 12/17/19%, terminal multiples 6/9/12 and growth 5/18/28% are assumptions, not management forecasts. They are sensitivity cases, not calibrated fair values, because tin economics and subsequent deployment remain unverified. R/D/P and IAS are NS. [S1][S2][S7] Model correction dated 20 October 2026: the earlier forecast omitted certain opening liabilities excluded from operating working capital. The revised model pays opening net tax and other current claims once, preserves actual opening assets/debt, and explicitly retains noncurrent employee claims in terminal equity with separate settlement sensitivities. This corrects our forecast, not the issuer’s financial statements. No liability is paid twice through working capital, debt, capex or recurring compensation. Corrected bear/base/bull terminal prices are ₹40.72/₹214.95/₹438.80; corresponding five-year returns are -19.03%/12.94%/30.26%. These remain conditional operating and funding scenarios, not executable entry prices. Opening-claim amounts, timing alternatives and annual cash/debt checks are in the model. [S1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Bear sequence: slower new-product adoption and commissioning delay lower utilization, reduce margins, trap stocks/receivables and require expensive funding despite IPO. Severe case adds 25% project overrun, falling revenue and 7% EBIT margin; terminal equity can approach zero, not an asset floor. Counterevidence is real existing utilization 90%, positive improving CFO and funded fresh equity.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A 5× in five years requires 37.97% annual per-share appreciation; 10× requires 58.49%. The verified three-year sales CAGR is 14.85%, and proposed tin capacity is not contracted revenue. Higher margins, rapid funded utilization and terminal valuation would all need to support these outcomes. No supported 5×/10× probability is assigned. [S1][S2]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Verify machinery order/delivery againstNovember–December 2026 schedule, January 2027 trial/commercial start and approvals. Reconcile project spent againstJuly 15.7564 crore and total 50.2123; material overrun needs funding reassessment. Track new tin orders separately from IML/end caps and keep capacity units distinct. Watch 6–12 month debtors 1.2997 crore and finished goods 6.9453 for actual realization. Monitor overdue charges 0.8173, MSME-interest recognition, related purchases and label supplier dependence. Obtain NCLT/ROC outcomes, current pledged shares and half-year utilization. Refresh quote, lot and executable depth before any allocation. [S1][S2][S6][S7]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Deep review covers annual/prospectus history, explicit restatement bridges, connected dealings, controls, funding, capital, operating economics, liquidity and linked valuation sensitivities. G1 no verified fail; G2 no critical hold because cash reconciles and major restatement bridges are disclosed. Medium quality-score confidence; investment valuation is low confidence and IAS unrankable. Modest source typos or procedural petitions are not presented as financial fraud.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Issuer-hosted final prospectus and revised September annual are principal sources; earlier annual and draft provide historical bridges. Primary five-year revenue anchor, postIPO deployment/commissioning, latest NCLT status and live BSE surveillance/depth remain unavailable after reasonable directory/public-search review. Secondary OHLCV explicitly distinguished from official security identity/lot. Proposed models separate assumptions from verified opening figures; no forecast WC ratio applied backward. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5][S6][S7][S8]
